perplexity.description:
The Lost Boys Original Motion Picture Soundtrack was released on July 31, 1987, by Atlantic Records as the official soundtrack to the vampire horror-comedy film of the same name. Comprising 10 songs across 36 minutes, the album captures the eclectic musical landscape of the late 1980s, blending rock, pop, and new wave styles that complemented the film's darkly comedic tone and youth-oriented narrative. The compilation features contributions from various artists rather than a single composer, reflecting the soundtrack's role as a cultural artifact of 1980s popular music.

The album's musical approach mirrors the film's blend of horror and humor, with tracks ranging from synth-driven new wave to hard rock, creating a sonic palette that appealed to both mainstream audiences and rock enthusiasts. This stylistic diversity made the soundtrack a significant commercial product of its era, capitalizing on the film's popularity among younger audiences during the height of the Brat Pack phenomenon. The soundtrack's success helped establish it as a notable entry in the 1980s horror-comedy genre, where music played an integral role in defining the film's cultural identity.

The Lost Boys soundtrack has maintained its status as a recognizable artifact of 1980s pop culture, evidenced by multiple vinyl reissues in subsequent decades, including audiophile-grade remastered editions released by Friday Music. These reissues underscore the album's enduring appeal to collectors and its continued relevance within discussions of 1980s soundtrack releases, cementing its place as a representative work of the era's approach to film music curation.
